instruction.text: Follow the dialogue between Ella and Darrel in the supermarket, then answer the following questions.

atoms.b: Hello, would you be interested in purchasing a reusable shopping bag?
Well, I already get these plastic bags every time I go shopping.
I see... may I ask you what you do with those bags once you’re done using them?
Not much. Sometimes I use them to bag other things, but most of the time I throw them away.
Yes, I understand. Did you know that about 90% of plastics that land in our oceans are single-use plastic items?
Definitely. According to current scientific findings, this amount of plastic greatly harms our marine life.
Wow, I didn’t know it was that bad...
Yes, exactly. That is why my organisation is trying to spread awareness and encourage consumers to do their part for our oceans. Are you interested in that shopping bag now? It’s only a pound.
Sure, that doesn’t sound like a bad idea now.

atoms.a: When someone is trying to convince you to do something, what kind of information should they give you?
b: ++Information that is as convincing as possible.
++Information that supports their claim or argument.

hint.text: There is more than one correct answer.

atoms.a: How would Ella’s claim sound if it were summarised?
b: ++Using reusable bags is better for our oceans than plastic bags.
Using plastic bags is just as good as using reusable bags.
A reusable tote bag just costs a pound.

feedback.end: A claim made by an author is the basis for the following facts and evidence.

atoms.a: What did Ella use in her argument to convince Darrel?
What would convincing evidence for using less plastic be?
b: ++Plastic waste often lands in water. 90% of plastic in oceans are single-use plastics.
Even though a lot of plastic lands in the ocean, almost all plastic is reused on land.
Using single-use plastic is nothing to worry about.

hint.text: The most important thing to do when reading a text is to figure out if the author is trying to convince you to do something and what they are trying to convince you to do. To convince their reader, authors use evidence and reason.

instruction.text: Find the evidence to use less single-use plastic in the text.

atoms.b: ((According to ANTON Science, millions of marine animals suffer plastic-related deaths yearly)). Marine life either becomes entangled by pieces of plastic and suffocates or accidentally swallows smaller pieces of plastic.

instruction.text: Find the reason to use less single-use plastic in the text.

atoms.b: The amount of single-use plastic items in our oceans such as straws, bottles and bags are growing with each passing day. ((This amount of plastic needs to be reduced as soon as possible to avoid further unnecessary animal deaths)).
